slot.brief: Four statements on adsorption (physisorption vs chemisorption, Freundlich log-log line slope, effect of temperature) – mark true/false combination

stem: Which of the following statements about adsorption is incorrect?
options: Physisorption becomes more pronounced with rise in temperature.
The value of $1/n$ in the Freundlich adsorption isotherm normally lies between 0 and 1.
Chemisorption is favoured at high temperature.
Adsorption is generally exothermic because it involves a decrease in surface energy.
notes: from question bank g4349a52fe992 (verified in job 20261127-122012-292e)
working:
A: Correct; Freundlich isotherm $x/m = k p^{1/n}$ has $1/n$ in (0,1).
B: Incorrect; Physisorption is exothermic, so it decreases with increasing temperature.
C: Correct; Chemisorption is often activated and favoured at high temperature.
D: Correct; Adsorption is exothermic as residual surface forces are satisfied and surface energy decreases.

Independent check: Physisorption is generally favored at lower temperatures, so it becomes less pronounced as temperature rises. The other listed statements are generally correct.
solution:
Physisorption is generally exothermic, so increasing temperature shifts the equilibrium toward desorption and reduces adsorption.
Chemisorption may be favoured at higher temperature because it often has an activation energy; the Freundlich exponent normally satisfies $0<1/n<1$.
Thus the incorrect statement is (A).
